answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the pearl identifier and voids the later submissions, so that the operator burns for 372 runs and collects one. Because the opal index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the lotus audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 372 answers need 372 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
